identity.name: Arthroscopy: The Journal of Arthroscopic and Related Surgery
identity.publisher: Elsevier (for the Arthroscopy Association of North America)
identity.source_note: Live guide is blocked to automated fetch (Cloudflare). source_hash is the SHA-256 of the normalized RAW Internet Archive snapshot of the official guide (web.archive.org/web/20230322id_/https://www.arthroscopyjournal.org/content/authorinfo, captured ~2023-03-22 (page footer 'Updated June 2020' — STALE, prioritize re-verification)) and is reproducible. Rules were encoded from this Internet Archive snapshot. Session C's freshness cron must use a headless fetch to re-verify the live page.

encoding_notes: Rules encoded from the official Arthroscopy 'Instructions for Authors' (arthroscopyjournal.org/content/authorinfo) via the Wayback Machine snapshot 2023-03-22 (page 'Updated June 2020'); the live page and the ScienceDirect Guide-for-Authors are bot-blocked to curl/WebFetch. source_hash is of the live page's Cloudflare challenge shell — see identity.source_note.

Peer review is explicitly double-blind: separate unblinded title page + blinded manuscript (blinded first page lists only the title; no author initials or institution names in text). scrub_metadata set true as an inference required for effective double-blind review (not stated verbatim).

article_types mapping: 'Original Article' -> original_research; 'Systematic Review' and 'Meta-analysis' -> systematic_review; 'Case Report (rarely accepted)' -> case_report; 'Letter to Editor & Reply' -> letter; 'Level V Evidence' (invited expert-opinion articles) -> editorial.

word_limits from the journal's 'Recommended Maximums' table. systematic_review encodes the Systematic Review row (4500 words); Meta-analysis (4000 words, same enum) noted here. Case Report shows '—' for all limits (rarely accepted, no stated caps) -> nulls. Word counts exclude title page, blinded title page, references, and figure legends.
'Technical Note' is NOT accepted in Arthroscopy itself (now published only in the companion journal Arthroscopy Techniques, video required) -> omitted from article_types.

abstract.sections reflect the Original Article structured abstract (Purpose/Methods/Results/Conclusions + Level of Evidence or Clinical Relevance). Case Reports and Level V Evidence use unstructured summary abstracts (noted via type, not abstract.sections which encodes the primary type).
No keywords requirement is stated in the guide -> keywords.required false; the journal does not mention ORCID, cover letter, or Highlights -> orcid/cover_letter false, highlights_required null.

references: journal follows the AMA Manual of Style / ICMJE Uniform Requirements; numbered in citation order; list all authors up to 6, then first 3 + 'et al' (et_al_threshold 6); journal names abbreviated per PubMed (mapped to 'nlm'). in_text 'superscript' inferred from AMA style (not stated verbatim). include_doi false: the standard periodical reference example omits a DOI (DOIs shown only for in-press and dataset references).

figures.formats left empty and min_dpi null: the fetched IFA does not list figure file formats or DPI (it defers to Elsevier artwork guidelines). Figures are submitted as separate files; legends supplied separately ('figure and video legends' section). Tables placed after references/legends in the submission order (grouped_end), title/caption above, numbered consecutively (arabic).

layout: guide specifies double spacing + continuous line numbering only. Font (Times New Roman 12) is a placeholder default — NOT specified by the guide; page size, margins, alignment, page numbers, and running head are also unspecified and defaulted to none/false/null for the engine to flag.

declarations: ICMJE disclosure forms are mandatory for every author (conflict_of_interest + funding required). IRB/ethics approval required for human studies (except retrospective/cadaver) and prospective clinical-trial registration required (on the title page) — both conditional, listed in order but not in 'required'.

Session-A consolidation (2026-07-09): supersedes any earlier note in this list that describes source_hash as a bot-challenge 'shell' hash or that records a placeholder body font/line-spacing. Authoritative current state: source_hash is reproducible per identity.source_note; font family/size and line-spacing are null wherever the live guide is silent, so the engine preserves the author's value rather than imposing a guess.
